title: "Yaad E Nana Akbar Zeeshan Morvi"
language: "Urdu"
lang: "ur"
direction: "ltr"
kalamType: "Other"
poet: "Zeeshan"
tags: ["noUrdu"]
aliases: []
published: false
---

1
Yaad Aate Hain Tumhein Dekh Ke Nana Akbar.
Dekh Loon Tum Ko Main Jee Bhar Ke Tu Jana Akbar.
Maa Ko Arman Hai Keh Dulha Bana Le Tum Ko.
Sehra Ik Bar Zara Sar Pe Sajana Akbar.

2
Gham Nahi Yeh Keh Chaley Jao Gay Maqtal Ki Taraf.
Gham Hai Keh Tum Ne Nahi Laut Ke Aana Akbar.
Aakhri Bar Main Nana Ki Ziyarat Kar Loon.
Sar Pe Dastar Pehan Kar Yeh Dikhana Akbar.

3
Jaisay Dar Fatima Zahra Ka Giraya Waisay.
Kalma Goyon Ne Tumhein Zeen Se Girana Akbar.
Waqt-e-Aakhir Kaha Akbar Ne Sisak Kar Baba.
Kehti Thi Sughra Mujhe Bhool Na Jana Akbar.

4
Ghutniyon Chalte Hoye Kehte They Ro Kar Shabeer.
Kitna Mushkil Hai Teri Lash Tak Aana Akbar.
Karbala Mein Karo Zeeshan-o- Asad Ko Bhi Talab.
Khon Hum Ne Hai Tere Gham Mein Bahana Akbar.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/yaad-e-nana-akbar-zeeshan-morvi-tajpoints-aec4a278af63b1ec54bd.md')
original = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{p}'], text=True).split('---', 2)[2].strip()
_, meta, body = p.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = '\\n'.join(line.removeprefix('  ') for line in meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1].strip('\\n').splitlines())
assert roman.casefold() == '\\n'.join(line.removesuffix('.') for line in original.splitlines()).casefold()
for edition, numerals in [(roman, '1234'), (body, '۱۲۳۴')]:
    blocks = [block.splitlines() for block in edition.strip().split('\\n\\n')]
    assert [block[0] for block in blocks] == list(numerals)
    assert all(len(block) == 5 for block in blocks)
assert '\\u200c' not in body
print('Verified four matched stanzas and 16 verses, with Roman wording preserved.')
PY

Reconstructed all 16 Urdu verses in the selected Markdown and verified that the four stanzas align with the Roman transcription preserved in `romanLyrics`. Set the direction to `rtl` and removed the `noUrdu` tag.

Read “tu” as تو (“then”) and rendered “Morvi” as موروی.
